items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1959-10-26
items.q: Although this man was a wonderful musician, he was a very talented musician, Benny Kruger.

ctx.x: That was a New York minister.

Yeah, a New York minister. He went to Albany and knocked us out of a job, forcing us relegated to a dance hall. We took the job in the dance hall. That almost took all the starch out of me. The Victor Company refused to record any more jazz. They made us put a saxophone in the band, and this thing almost ruined the band. Never gave us the right, although, write kind of music. Although this man was a wonderful musician, he was a very talented musician, Benny Kruger. But nobody wanted to record jazz no more, only…

items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: It was Benny Kruger. Benny Kruger. One of the most versatile men in New York at the time. Yes sir. But he was not a jazz man.

ctx.x: And that's immediately upon coming back from London. That's right. Robertson Hilton. And then what was the name of the saxophone players? I want to get that to you.
It was Benny Kruger. Benny Kruger. One of the most versatile men in New York at the time. Yes sir. But he was not a jazz man.
So now back to Gilda Gray and her shimmy.
